sanskrit: naiṣa śakyo hi saṃgrāme jetuṃ bhūtena kena cit tatra gacchata bhadraṃ vo rājānaṃ parirakṣata
english: "This one cannot be conquered in battle by any living creature. Go there, good fortune to you, and guard the king well.

sanskrit: abhidrutaṃ mahābhāgaṃ rākṣasena durātmanā etad dhi paramaṃ kṛtyaṃ sarveṣāṃ naḥ paraṃtapāḥ
english: The illustrious king is hard pressed by that wicked-souled rākṣasa. This, O scorchers of foes, is now the foremost duty of us all."

sanskrit: pitāmahavacaḥ śrutvā tvaramāṇā mahārathāḥ uttamaṃ javam āsthāya prayayur yatra kauravaḥ
english: Hearing the grandsire's words, the great chariot-warriors made haste and, summoning their utmost speed, rushed to where the Kaurava stood.

sanskrit: droṇaś ca somadattaś ca bāhlikaś ca jayadrathaḥ kṛpo bhūriśravāḥ śalyaś citraseno viviṃśatiḥ
english: Droṇa and Somadatta and Bāhlika and Jayadratha, Kṛpa, Bhūriśravas, Śalya, Citrasena, Viviṃśati—

sanskrit: aśvatthāmā vikarṇaś ca āvantyaś ca bṛhadbalaḥ rathāś cānekasāhasrā ye teṣām anuyāyinaḥ abhidrutaṃ parīpsantaḥ putraṃ duryodhanaṃ tava
english: Aśvatthāman and Vikarṇa, the prince of Avanti and Bṛhadbala, and the many thousands of chariots that followed them—all seeking to rescue your hard-pressed son Duryodhana.

sanskrit: tad anīkam anādhṛṣyaṃ pālitaṃ lokasattamaiḥ ātatāyinam āyāntaṃ prekṣya rākṣasasattamaḥ nākampata mahābāhur maināka iva parvataḥ
english: Beholding that unassailable host, guarded by the foremost men of the world, advancing upon him with weapons drawn, the best of rākṣasas, mighty-armed, did not waver—like the mountain Maināka.

sanskrit: pragṛhya vipulaṃ cāpaṃ jñātibhiḥ parivāritaḥ śūlamudgarahastaiś ca nānāpraharaṇair api
english: Grasping his vast bow, surrounded by his kinsmen, who bore spears and maces in their hands and weapons of every kind,

sanskrit: tataḥ samabhavad yuddhaṃ tumulaṃ lomaharṣaṇam rākṣasānāṃ ca mukhyasya duryodhanabalasya ca
english: there arose a tumultuous, hair-raising battle between the chief of the rākṣasas and the army of Duryodhana.

sanskrit: dhanuṣāṃ kūjatāṃ śabdaḥ sarvatas tumulo 'bhavat aśrūyata mahārāja vaṃśānāṃ dahyatām iva
english: The twanging clamor of the bows rose tumultuous on every side; it was heard, O great king, like the crackling of bamboos burning in a fire.

sanskrit: śastrāṇāṃ pātyamānānāṃ kavaceṣu śarīriṇām śabdaḥ samabhavad rājann adrīṇām iva dīryatām
english: From the weapons falling upon the armor of embodied warriors there arose a sound, O king, like that of mountains splitting asunder.

sanskrit: vīrabāhuvisṛṣṭānāṃ tomarāṇāṃ viśāṃ pate rūpam āsīd viyatsthānāṃ sarpāṇāṃ sarpatām iva
english: The javelins hurled by the arms of heroes, as they coursed through the sky, O lord of peoples, had the look of serpents gliding aloft.

sanskrit: tataḥ paramasaṃkruddho visphārya sumahad dhanuḥ rākṣasendro mahābāhur vinadan bhairavaṃ ravam
english: Then, supremely enraged, the mighty-armed lord of rākṣasas drew his enormous bow taut and let loose a terrible roar.

sanskrit: ācāryasyārdhacandreṇa kruddhaś ciccheda kārmukam somadattasya bhallena dhvajam unmathya cānadat
english: In his wrath he cut through the teacher's bow with a crescent-headed arrow, and with a broad shaft he struck down Somadatta's banner and roared aloud.

sanskrit: bāhlikaṃ ca tribhir bāṇair abhyavidhyat stanāntare kṛpam ekena vivyādha citrasenaṃ tribhiḥ śaraiḥ
english: He pierced Bāhlika between the breasts with three arrows, struck Kṛpa with one, and Citrasena with three shafts.

sanskrit: pūrṇāyatavisṛṣṭena samyak praṇihitena ca jatrudeśe samāsādya vikarṇaṃ samatāḍayat nyaṣīdat sa rathopasthe śoṇitena pariplutaḥ
english: With a shaft drawn to the full and well aimed, reaching Vikarṇa at the collarbone, he smote him; and Vikarṇa sank down upon the floor of his chariot, drenched in blood.

sanskrit: tataḥ punar ameyātmā nārācān daśa pañca ca bhūriśravasi saṃkruddhaḥ prāhiṇod bharatarṣabha te varma bhittvā tasyāśu prāviśan medinītalam
english: Then again the immeasurable-souled one, enraged, loosed fifteen iron shafts at Bhūriśravas, O bull of the Bharatas; and they, piercing his armor, swiftly passed on and entered the surface of the earth.

sanskrit: viviṃśateś ca drauṇeś ca yantārau samatāḍayat tau petatū rathopasthe raśmīn utsṛjya vājinām
english: He struck the charioteers of Viviṃśati and of Droṇa's son, and both fell upon the floors of their chariots, letting go the reins of their horses.

sanskrit: sindhurājño 'rdhacandreṇa vārāhaṃ svarṇabhūṣitam unmamātha mahārāja dvitīyenācchinad dhanuḥ
english: With a crescent-headed arrow he tore down the gold-adorned boar-emblem of the king of the Sindhus, O great king, and with a second he severed his bow.

sanskrit: caturbhir atha nārācair āvantyasya mahātmanaḥ jaghāna caturo vāhān krodhasaṃraktalocanaḥ
english: Then with four iron shafts, his eyes red with wrath, he slew the four horses of the high-souled prince of Avanti.

sanskrit: pūrṇāyatavisṛṣṭena pītena niśitena ca nirbibheda mahārāja rājaputraṃ bṛhadbalam sa gāḍhaviddho vyathito rathopastha upāviśat
english: With a sharp, yellow shaft drawn to the full, he pierced through the prince Bṛhadbala, O great king; and he, sorely wounded and shaken, sank down within his chariot.

sanskrit: bhṛśaṃ krodhena cāviṣṭo rathastho rākṣasādhipaḥ cikṣepa niśitāṃs tīkṣṇāñ śarān āśīviṣopamān bibhidus te mahārāja śalyaṃ yuddhaviśāradam
english: Then, deeply possessed by wrath, the lord of rākṣasas, mounted on his chariot, hurled sharp, keen arrows like venomous serpents; and these, O great king, pierced Śalya, skilled in war.

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca vimukhīkṛtya tān sarvāṃs tāvakān yudhi rākṣasaḥ jighāṃsur bharataśreṣṭha duryodhanam upādravat
english: Saṃjaya said: Having turned back all your warriors in the fight, the rākṣasa, eager to slay, rushed upon Duryodhana, O best of the Bharatas.

sanskrit: tam āpatantaṃ saṃprekṣya rājānaṃ prati vegitam abhyadhāvaj jighāṃsantas tāvakā yuddhadurmadāḥ
english: Seeing him charging swiftly upon the king, your warriors, frenzied for battle, rushed forward eager to kill him.

sanskrit: tālamātrāṇi cāpāni vikarṣanto mahābalāḥ tam ekam abhyadhāvanta nadantaḥ siṃhasaṃghavat
english: Drawing their bows tall as palm trees, those men of great might rushed upon him alone, roaring like a troop of lions.

sanskrit: athainaṃ śaravarṣeṇa samantāt paryavārayan parvataṃ vāridhārābhiḥ śaradīva balāhakāḥ
english: Then they hemmed him in on every side with a torrent of arrows, as autumn clouds enshroud a mountain with their downpour of rain.

sanskrit: sa gāḍhaviddho vyathitas tottrārdita iva dvipaḥ utpapāta tadākāśaṃ samantād vainateyavat
english: Sorely wounded and pained, like an elephant goaded by the driver's hook, he sprang up into the sky on every side like the son of Vinatā.

sanskrit: vyanadat sumahānādaṃ jīmūta iva śāradaḥ diśaḥ khaṃ pradiśaś caiva nādayan bhairavasvanaḥ
english: He let forth a mighty roar like an autumn thundercloud, his terrible voice making the quarters, the sky, and the intermediate regions resound.

sanskrit: rākṣasasya tu taṃ śabdaṃ śrutvā rājā yudhiṣṭhiraḥ uvāca bharataśreṣṭho bhīmasenam idaṃ vacaḥ
english: Hearing that roar of the rākṣasa, king Yudhiṣṭhira, the best of the Bharatas, spoke these words to Bhīmasena:

sanskrit: yudhyate rākṣaso nūnaṃ dhārtarāṣṭrair mahārathaiḥ yathāsya śrūyate śabdo nadato bhairavaṃ svanam atibhāraṃ ca paśyāmi tatra tāta samāhitam
english: "Surely the rākṣasa is fighting against the great chariot-warriors of Dhṛtarāṣṭra's son, as one hears his cry roaring with a terrible voice. I perceive, dear one, that a grievous burden has fallen upon him there.

sanskrit: pitāmahaś ca saṃkruddhaḥ pāñcālān hantum udyataḥ teṣāṃ ca rakṣaṇārthāya yudhyate phalgunaḥ paraiḥ
english: And the grandsire, enraged, is bent upon destroying the Pāñcālas; and Phalguna, to protect them, fights against the foes.

sanskrit: etac chrutvā mahābāho kāryadvayam upasthitam gaccha rakṣasva haiḍimbaṃ saṃśayaṃ paramaṃ gatam
english: Hearing of this, O mighty-armed one, two tasks press upon us. Go and protect the son of Hiḍimbā, who has come into the gravest peril."

sanskrit: bhrātur vacanam ājñāya tvaramāṇo vṛkodaraḥ prayayau siṃhanādena trāsayan sarvapārthivān vegena mahatā rājan parvakāle yathodadhiḥ
english: Heeding his brother's word, Vṛkodara hastened forth, terrifying all the kings with his lion's roar, and with great speed, O king, like the ocean at the time of the new moon.

sanskrit: tam anvayāt satyadhṛtiḥ saucittir yuddhadurmadaḥ śreṇimān vasudānaś ca putraḥ kāśyasya cābhibhūḥ
english: Satyadhṛti followed him, and the son of Sucitti, mad for battle, and Śreṇimān and Vasudāna, and the son of the king of Kāśi, Abhibhū.

sanskrit: abhimanyumukhāś caiva draupadeyā mahārathāḥ kṣatradevaś ca vikrāntaḥ kṣatradharmā tathaiva ca
english: And the sons of Draupadī, great chariot-warriors led by Abhimanyu, and the valiant Kṣatradeva, and Kṣatradharman likewise,

sanskrit: anūpādhipatiś caiva nīlaḥ svabalam āsthitaḥ mahatā rathavaṃśena haiḍimbaṃ paryavārayan
english: and the lord of Anūpa, Nīla, stationed amid his own forces—with a great array of chariots they surrounded the son of Hiḍimbā.

sanskrit: kuñjaraiś ca sadā mattaiḥ ṣaṭsahasraiḥ prahāribhiḥ abhyarakṣanta sahitā rākṣasendraṃ ghaṭotkacam
english: And with six thousand ever-rutting, war-striking elephants, joined together, they guarded the lord of rākṣasas, Ghaṭotkaca.

sanskrit: siṃhanādena mahatā nemighoṣeṇa caiva hi khuraśabdaninādaiś ca kampayanto vasuṃdharām
english: With a great lion-roar, with the rumble of chariot-wheel rims, and with the thunder of hoofbeats, they made the earth tremble.

sanskrit: teṣām āpatatāṃ śrutvā śabdaṃ taṃ tāvakaṃ balam bhīmasenabhayodvignaṃ vivarṇavadanaṃ tathā parivṛttaṃ mahārāja parityajya ghaṭotkacam
english: Hearing the noise of their onset, your host, agitated by fear of Bhīmasena and pale of face, turned and fled, O great king, abandoning Ghaṭotkaca.

sanskrit: tataḥ pravavṛte yuddhaṃ tatra tatra mahātmanām tāvakānāṃ pareṣāṃ ca saṃgrāmeṣv anivartinām
english: Then the battle broke out here and there among those high-souled men, your warriors and the foes alike, who never turned back in combat.

sanskrit: nānārūpāṇi śastrāṇi visṛjanto mahārathāḥ anyonyam abhidhāvantaḥ saṃprahāraṃ pracakrire vyatiṣaktaṃ mahāraudraṃ yuddhaṃ bhīrubhayāvaham
english: Loosing weapons of every kind, the great chariot-warriors rushed upon one another and joined in a clash—a tangled, most terrible fight, fraught with terror for the faint of heart.

sanskrit: hayā gajaiḥ samājagmuḥ pādātā rathibhiḥ saha anyonyaṃ samare rājan prārthayānā mahad yaśaḥ
english: Horses closed with elephants, foot-soldiers with charioteers, each seeking great glory against the other in the fight, O king.

sanskrit: sahasā cābhavat tīvraṃ saṃnipātān mahad rajaḥ rathāśvagajapattīnāṃ padanemisamuddhatam
english: And of a sudden, from that collision, there arose a thick, dense dust, churned up by the feet and wheel-rims of chariots, horses, elephants, and infantry.

sanskrit: dhūmrāruṇaṃ rajas tīvraṃ raṇabhūmiṃ samāvṛṇot naiva sve na pare rājan samajānan parasparam
english: The dense dust, smoke-gray and red, covered over the field of battle; and neither one's own men nor the foe, O king, could recognize one another.

sanskrit: pitā putraṃ na jānīte putro vā pitaraṃ tathā nirmaryāde tathā bhūte vaiśase lomaharṣaṇe
english: Father knew not son, nor son his father, in that hair-raising carnage where all bounds were broken.

sanskrit: śastrāṇāṃ bharataśreṣṭha manuṣyāṇāṃ ca garjatām sumahān abhavac chabdo vaṃśānām iva dahyatām
english: Of the weapons and of the men crying aloud there rose a mighty din, O best of the Bharatas, like that of bamboos burning in a fire.

sanskrit: gajavājimanuṣyāṇāṃ śoṇitāntrataraṅgiṇī prāvartata nadī tatra keśaśaivalaśādvalā
english: A river streamed there with waves of the blood and entrails of elephants, horses, and men, its weeds and grasses made of human hair.

sanskrit: narāṇāṃ caiva kāyebhyaḥ śirasāṃ patatāṃ raṇe śuśruve sumahāñ śabdaḥ patatām aśmanām iva
english: As the heads of men fell from their bodies in the battle, a very great sound was heard, like that of falling stones.

sanskrit: viśiraskair manuṣyaiś ca chinnagātraiś ca vāraṇaiḥ aśvaiḥ saṃbhinnadehaiś ca saṃkīrṇābhūd vasuṃdharā
english: With headless men, with elephants whose limbs were severed, and with horses whose bodies were torn apart, the earth was strewn over.

sanskrit: nānāvidhāni śastrāṇi visṛjanto mahārathāḥ anyonyam abhidhāvantaḥ saṃprahāraṃ pracakrire
english: Loosing weapons of many kinds, the great chariot-warriors rushed upon one another and joined in the clash of arms.

sanskrit: hayā hayān samāsādya preṣitā hayasādibhiḥ samāhatya raṇe 'nyonyaṃ nipetur gatajīvitāḥ
english: Horses, urged on by their riders, met other horses and, striking against one another in the fight, fell down with their lives fled.

sanskrit: narā narān samāsādya krodharaktekṣaṇā bhṛśam urāṃsy urobhir anyonyaṃ samāśliṣya nijaghnire
english: Men met men, their eyes deeply red with wrath, and pressing breast against breast they grappled and slew one another.

sanskrit: preṣitāś ca mahāmātrair vāraṇāḥ paravāraṇāḥ abhighnanti viṣāṇāgrair vāraṇān eva saṃyuge
english: Driven on by their mahouts, elephants struck the enemy's elephants, smiting those elephants in the fray with the tips of their tusks.

sanskrit: te jātarudhirāpīḍāḥ patākābhir alaṃkṛtāḥ saṃsaktāḥ pratyadṛśyanta meghā iva savidyutaḥ
english: Streaming with welling blood and adorned with banners, locked together they looked like clouds shot through with lightning.

sanskrit: ke cid bhinnā viṣāṇāgrair bhinnakumbhāś ca tomaraiḥ vinadanto 'bhyadhāvanta garjanto jaladā iva
english: Some, pierced by tusk-tips and their frontal globes broken by javelins, charged about trumpeting, roaring like rain-clouds.

sanskrit: ke cid dhastair dvidhā chinnaiś chinnagātrās tathāpare nipetus tumule tasmiṃś chinnapakṣā ivādrayaḥ
english: Some, their trunks cut in two, and others with their limbs severed, fell in that tumult like mountains shorn of their wings.

sanskrit: pārśvais tu dāritair anye vāraṇair varavāraṇāḥ mumucuḥ śoṇitaṃ bhūri dhātūn iva mahīdharāḥ
english: Other splendid elephants, their flanks rent open by the foe's elephants, poured forth blood in floods, like mountains streaming with their ores.

sanskrit: nārācābhihatās tv anye tathā viddhāś ca tomaraiḥ hatārohā vyadṛśyanta viśṛṅgā iva parvatāḥ
english: Others, struck by iron shafts and pierced by javelins, their riders slain, appeared like mountains shorn of their peaks.

sanskrit: ke cit krodhasamāviṣṭā madāndhā niravagrahāḥ rathān hayān padātāṃś ca mamṛduḥ śataśo raṇe
english: Some, possessed by rage, blind with rut and unrestrained, crushed chariots, horses, and footmen by the hundred in the battle.

sanskrit: tathā hayā hayārohais tāḍitāḥ prāsatomaraiḥ tena tenābhyavartanta kurvanto vyākulā diśaḥ
english: And horses, struck by their riders with lances and javelins, wheeled this way and that, throwing the quarters into confusion.

sanskrit: rathino rathibhiḥ sārdhaṃ kulaputrās tanutyajaḥ parāṃ śaktiṃ samāsthāya cakruḥ karmāṇy abhītavat
english: Chariot-warriors against chariot-warriors, men of noble birth ready to give up their bodies, putting forth their utmost strength, performed deeds without fear.

sanskrit: svayaṃvara ivāmarde prajahrur itaretaram prārthayānā yaśo rājan svargaṃ vā yuddhaśālinaḥ
english: In that carnage they struck at one another as at a bridegroom's choosing, those skilled in war seeking glory, O king, or else heaven.

sanskrit: tasmiṃs tathā vartamāne saṃgrāme lomaharṣaṇe dhārtarāṣṭraṃ mahat sainyaṃ prāyaśo vimukhīkṛtam
english: As that hair-raising battle raged on, the great army of Dhṛtarāṣṭra's son was for the most part turned to flight.

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca svasainyaṃ nihataṃ dṛṣṭvā rājā duryodhanaḥ svayam abhyadhāvata saṃkruddho bhīmasenam ariṃdamam
english: Saṃjaya said: Seeing his own army slaughtered, king Duryodhana himself, enraged, rushed against Bhīmasena, the tamer of foes.

sanskrit: pragṛhya sumahac cāpam indrāśanisamasvanam mahatā śaravarṣeṇa pāṇḍavaṃ samavākirat
english: Grasping his enormous bow, whose twang was like the thunderbolt of Indra, he covered the Pāṇḍava with a great torrent of arrows.

sanskrit: ardhacandraṃ ca saṃdhāya sutīkṣṇaṃ lomavāhinam bhīmasenasya ciccheda cāpaṃ krodhasamanvitaḥ
english: And fitting to his bow a very sharp, feathered crescent-headed shaft, filled with wrath, he severed Bhīmasena's bow.

sanskrit: tadantaraṃ ca saṃprekṣya tvaramāṇo mahārathaḥ saṃdadhe niśitaṃ bāṇaṃ girīṇām api dāraṇam tenorasi mahābāhur bhīmasenam atāḍayat
english: Seeing his opening, the great chariot-warrior in haste fitted a keen arrow that could cleave even mountains, and with it the mighty-armed one struck Bhīmasena upon the chest.

sanskrit: sa gāḍhaviddho vyathitaḥ sṛkkiṇī parisaṃlihan samālalambe tejasvī dhvajaṃ hemapariṣkṛtam
english: Sorely wounded and pained, the splendid warrior, licking the corners of his mouth, clung to his gold-wrought banner-staff.

sanskrit: tathā vimanasaṃ dṛṣṭvā bhīmasenaṃ ghaṭotkacaḥ krodhenābhiprajajvāla didhakṣann iva pāvakaḥ
english: Seeing Bhīmasena thus distressed, Ghaṭotkaca blazed up with wrath, like a fire about to consume all.

sanskrit: abhimanyumukhāś caiva pāṇḍavānāṃ mahārathāḥ samabhyadhāvan krośanto rājānaṃ jātasaṃbhramāḥ
english: And the great chariot-warriors of the Pāṇḍavas, led by Abhimanyu, charged forward shouting, agitated, upon the king.

sanskrit: saṃprekṣya tān āpatataḥ saṃkruddhāñ jātasaṃbhramān bhāradvājo 'bravīd vākyaṃ tāvakānāṃ mahārathān
english: Seeing them rushing on, enraged and agitated, the son of Bharadvāja spoke these words to your great chariot-warriors:

sanskrit: kṣipraṃ gacchata bhadraṃ vo rājānaṃ parirakṣata saṃśayaṃ paramaṃ prāptaṃ majjantaṃ vyasanārṇave
english: "Go swiftly, good fortune to you, and protect the king, who has come into the gravest peril and is sinking in an ocean of distress.

sanskrit: ete kruddhā maheṣvāsāḥ pāṇḍavānāṃ mahārathāḥ bhīmasenaṃ puraskṛtya duryodhanam upadrutāḥ
english: These enraged, mighty bowmen, the great chariot-warriors of the Pāṇḍavas, with Bhīmasena at their head, have fallen upon Duryodhana,

sanskrit: nānāvidhāni śastrāṇi visṛjanto jaye ratāḥ nadanto bhairavān nādāṃs trāsayantaś ca bhūm imām
english: loosing weapons of every kind, intent on victory, roaring terrible roars and making this earth tremble."

sanskrit: tad ācāryavacaḥ śrutvā somadattapurogamāḥ tāvakāḥ samavartanta pāṇḍavānām anīkinīm
english: Hearing those words of the teacher, your warriors, with Somadatta at their head, turned upon the host of the Pāṇḍavas.

sanskrit: kṛpo bhūriśravāḥ śalyo droṇaputro viviṃśatiḥ citraseno vikarṇaś ca saindhavo 'tha bṛhadbalaḥ āvantyau ca maheṣvāsau kauravaṃ paryavārayan
english: Kṛpa, Bhūriśravas, Śalya, Droṇa's son, Viviṃśati, Citrasena and Vikarṇa, then the lord of the Sindhus and Bṛhadbala, and the two mighty bowmen of Avanti—these surrounded the Kaurava king.

sanskrit: te viṃśatipadaṃ gatvā saṃprahāraṃ pracakrire pāṇḍavā dhārtarāṣṭrāś ca parasparajighāṃsavaḥ
english: Having advanced twenty paces, the Pāṇḍavas and the sons of Dhṛtarāṣṭra joined in the clash, each seeking to slay the other.

sanskrit: evam uktvā mahābāhur mahad visphārya kārmukam bhāradvājas tato bhīmaṃ ṣaḍviṃśatyā samārpayat
english: Having spoken thus, the mighty-armed son of Bharadvāja drew his great bow taut and then struck Bhīma with twenty-six arrows.

sanskrit: bhūyaś cainaṃ mahābāhuḥ śaraiḥ śīghram avākirat parvataṃ vāridhārābhiḥ śaradīva balāhakaḥ
english: And again the mighty-armed one swiftly covered him with arrows, as an autumn cloud enshrouds a mountain with its downpour of rain.

sanskrit: taṃ pratyavidhyad daśabhir bhīmasenaḥ śilīmukhaiḥ tvaramāṇo maheṣvāsaḥ savye pārśve mahābalaḥ
english: Bhīmasena struck him back with ten arrows—that mighty bowman of great strength, in haste, upon the left side.

sanskrit: sa gāḍhaviddho vyathito vayovṛddhaś ca bhārata pranaṣṭasaṃjñaḥ sahasā rathopastha upāviśat
english: Sorely wounded and pained, and aged withal, O Bhārata, his senses suddenly lost, he sank down upon the floor of his chariot.
